gro_006: You can recognise it by its tall, narrow crown, bred to fit into a gap between buildings barely wider than the tree itself. It stands in the Engelenpoortje alley, between Poelestraat and Nieuwe Markt.
gro_007: You can recognise it by its thinning crown but intact trunk base, standing alone at the centre of the square. It stands in Martinikerkhof, in the shadow of the Martini Tower.
gro_008: You can recognise it by growing inside the walled Prinsentuin garden, reached through the gate topped with a working 1731 sundial. It stands in the Prinsentuin, entrance on Turfsingel.
gro_009: You can recognise it by the extra room deliberately cleared around it during the square's recent redevelopment. It stands in the open around the Akerk church on Akerkhof.
gro_010: You can recognise it by its bark shedding in flaking plates like a plane tree's, unusual among maples. It stands on Guyotplein, beside the 1829 monument to Henri Daniel Guyot.
gro_011: You can recognise it by its cascading branches sweeping down and outward into a green curtain, visible through a glass wall built to keep the view. It stands in the Oude Hortus.
gro_012: You can recognise it by its height, about 29 metres, and trunk just over 4 metres round, on a corner plot beside the garden's newer building. It stands in the Oude Hortus.
gro_013: You can recognise it by its three stems and fan-shaped leaves, the thickest ginkgo trunk anywhere in Groningen. It stands close to the former Botanical Laboratory site in the Oude Hortus.
gro_017: You can recognise it by its slight lean against the building's facade, roots visibly pushing and cracking the wall beside it. It stands on Oosterweg in front of the Poortershoes.
gro_018: You can recognise it by the dozens of small knobbly regrowth points ringing its base, scars from repeated pollarding over the decades. It stands on the corner of Wilhelminakade and Oranjesingel.
gro_019: You can recognise it by the bench circling its base on a small corner playground. It stands at Verlengde Oosterweg 2, where three streets meet.
gro_020: You can recognise them by their trunks trained flat and pollarded into shape, ten hollow with visible tie rods from 1980s repairs. They fill the courtyard of the Pepergasthuis on Peperstraat.
